snippet.title: Encuentro entre Michael Jackson y la Princesa Diana en 1988 - Subtitulado en Español
snippet.description:
El 16 de Julio de 1988  Michael se encuentra con la pareja real entre bastidores del Bad Tour en Wembley Londres para presentarles un cheque de 450 mil dolares  de parte del del príncipe y otro cheque de 100 mil  eurosal Great Ormond Street Children's Hospital y tambien 13 de Septiembre de 1997, Michael asiste a una misa en memoria de la Princesa Diana en la Iglesia Episcopal St. James de Los Angeles.
El 3 de septiembre de 1997 Michael dedica el concierto que celebraba ese día en Ostend, Bélgica, a la Princesa Diana de Gales, fallecida el 31 de agosto en París. Originalmente, el concierto se iba a celebrar el día 1 de septiembre pero tras oír la noticia, Michael decidió cancelarlo. En la actuación de este día, le dedicó especialmente Heal the world al ser también una gran humanitaria. A partir de ese concierto de la gira History, antes de comenzar cada uno de los que le siguieron se reproducía en las pantallas gigantes la canción Smile con imágenes de la Princesa. Debido a la tragedia, Michael envió un comunicado de prensa: “La repentina pérdida de la Princesa de Gales, Diana, es unas de las tragedias más grandes del milenio. Era amiga del mundo. 

La he seguido durante toda mi vida. Hablo con autoridad cuando digo que estoy horrorizado de que los paparazzi, apoyados por sus publicaciones, hayan tenido un comportamiento tan salvaje y no puede ser aceptado por el público. Así no podemos garantizar una sociedad civilizada. Si la gente sigue aceptando estas prácticas, aceleramos la consecución de tragedias con esta magnitud”.

En la canción Privacy de su album Invincible de 2001 habla sobre ella:

Algunos de Ustedes aun se preguntaran por que una de mis amigas tuvo que morir
Para transmitir un mensaje que sin embargo no han oido
Mi amiga fue perseguida y confundida, como muchos otros que yo conocía
Pero en aquella fría noche de invierno, me arrebataron mi orgullo
Ahora ella no tiene una segunda oportunidad, es ridiculizada y acosada
Por favor, diganme por que?

En el video incluí parte de el documental Private Home Movies y un reportaje con escenas de la entrevista con Barbara Walters.

snippet.title: Michael Jackson & Princess Diana: One Unforgettable Night ❤️
snippet.description:
For one unforgettable night, two icons from completely different worlds stood under the same spotlight.

On July 16, 1988, Princess Diana and Prince Charles attended Michael Jackson’s Bad Tour concert at Wembley Stadium in London.

Michael knew Diana would be in the audience. Wanting to show respect, he reportedly removed “Dirty Diana” from the setlist.

But Diana had a surprise for him.

She told Michael that “Dirty Diana” was one of her favorite songs and asked why he had left it out.

Michael eventually performed it.

After the concert, the two icons shared a memorable meeting. Their worlds could hardly have been more different—one was the King of Pop, the other one of the most famous members of the British royal family.

Yet both understood what it meant to live under constant cameras, enormous public attention, and almost unimaginable fame.

Years later, their connection would be remembered as one of the most fascinating encounters between music and royalty.

Two legends. One night. One unforgettable meeting.

On July 16, 1988, Princess Diana and Prince Charles attended Michael Jackson’s Bad World Tour concert at Wembley Stadium in London.

Then Diana surprised him.

She reportedly told Michael that “Dirty Diana” was one of her favorite songs and asked him not to leave it out.

So Michael performed it.

That night brought together two of the most recognizable figures in the world: the King of Pop and one of the most famous members of the British royal family.

Although their face-to-face meetings were limited, biographical accounts describe later phone conversations between them and a friendship that developed afterward.

The Wembley photograph therefore captures more than a celebrity meeting.

It captures the moment two completely different worlds crossed paths—and one unforgettable song became part of the story.

July 16, 1988. Wembley Stadium. 72,000 people. Michael Jackson at the height of the Bad era. 🖤🔥

This footage comes from one of the most famous concerts of Michael Jackson’s legendary Bad World Tour—his sold-out performance at Wembley Stadium in London on July 16, 1988.

The audience included two very special guests: Diana, Princess of Wales, and Charles, Prince of Wales. The official release of the concert confirms that 72,000 people filled Wembley Stadium that night. 

The concert became particularly memorable because Jackson met the royal couple backstage shortly before the show. He presented them with special Bad Tour jackets for their family, including jackets intended for the young Princes William and Harry. Jackson also participated in a charitable presentation involving the Prince’s Trust and a children's hospital. 

One of the most famous stories from the night involves “Dirty Diana.” Jackson had reportedly considered removing the song from the set because Princess Diana would be attending. However, Diana told him that “Dirty Diana” was one of her favorite songs, and the song ultimately appeared in the performance. She and Charles were therefore in the audience when Jackson performed it. 

The setlist demonstrates just how extraordinary Jackson's live show had become. He opened with “Wanna Be Startin’ Somethin’”, followed by “This Place Hotel,” “Another Part of Me,” “I Just Can’t Stop Loving You,” “She’s Out of My Life,” the Jackson 5 medley, “Rock With You,” “Human Nature,” and “Smooth Criminal.”

The second half became even more spectacular, featuring “Dirty Diana,” “Thriller,” “Working Day and Night,” “Beat It,” “Billie Jean,” “Bad,” and the emotional encore, “Man in the Mirror.” 

Interestingly, because the show started late following Jackson's meeting with the royal couple, “The Way You Make Me Feel” was not performed that night. The version included as a bonus on the later DVD came from another Wembley performance. 

Jackson's Wembley concerts became a major milestone of the Bad Tour. He eventually performed seven sold-out shows at Wembley in 1988, drawing approximately 504,000 people altogether.
